# Coupled enlargement on one actual shared support face

This note treats convex POLYGONS A,K,B. It proves an exact compatible
body variation and its cap-budget cost. No reduction of general
minimizers to polygons is claimed. In particular, a middle face larger
than its endpoint Minkowski face is retained, with its actual cap
signatures and an explicit possible cost penalty.

## 1. Actual three-fiber data and the shared face

Use the planar finite-menu setup of
`candidate 6e9992972c414d73`.
There are exactly three full-dimensional fibers A,K,B at -1,0,1,
with (A+B)/2 subset K. Three actual equal-budget caps through
(0,y_0), y_0 in int K, have spanning normals v_i with sum v_i=0,
proper A and K cuts, and B support thresholds h_i=h_B(v_i).
Their A thresholds are b_i=2v_i.y_0-h_i and their middle thresholds
are v_i.y_0. Put

    s_i=2sigma_Ai+sigma_Ki,
    p_i=(1/s_i)/(sum_j 1/s_j),
    W_A(x)=sum_i p_i 1_(v_i.x>=b_i),
    W_K(x)=sum_i p_i 1_(v_i.x>=v_i.y_0).

Both loads lie between min p_i>0 and 1, since the corresponding
three halfspaces cover the plane. Write Q for their common raw mass,
M=|A|+|K|+|B|, and r=Q/M.

Let n be an outward unit normal with the ACTUAL support equality

    h_A(n)+h_B(n)=2h_K(n).                           (1)

Let F_A,F_B,F_K be the exposed faces in this direction. Assume F_A
is a nondegenerate edge. F_B is an edge or a point; let its length
be L_B, allowing L_B=0. Write L_A,L_K for the lengths of the other
two faces. Midpoint compatibility gives

    I_0=(F_A+F_B)/2 subset F_K,
    L_K>=(L_A+L_B)/2.                                (2)

Choose ANY p in relint F_A and define actual new fibers

    A_epsilon=conv(A union {p+epsilon n}),
    K_epsilon=conv(K union (A_epsilon+B)/2),
    B_epsilon=B.                                    (3)

They remain compatible by definition. Their labeled convex hull has
exactly these integer fibers; all three fibers remain full-dimensional.

## 2. The added A triangle and K trapezoid are exact

For all sufficiently small epsilon>0, A_epsilon minus A is exactly
the triangle over F_A with apex p+epsilon n, apart from its base.
Indeed p strictly satisfies every other facet inequality of A, and
the same holds for its small outward displacement.

There is also an exact, not merely asymptotic, description of the
middle addition. Put J=(p+F_B)/2, a segment of length L_B/2 or a point.
Then for all sufficiently small epsilon,

    K_epsilon=conv(K union (J+epsilon n/2)).          (4)

To prove this, Minkowski addition distributes over convex hull, so
the only additional seed for K is (p+epsilon n+B)/2. For any facet
normal u of K not positively proportional to n, p in relint F_A
implies u.p<h_A(u): the only supporting unit normal of A at p is n.
Thus every point of (p+B)/2 satisfies

    u.(p+B)/2 <=[u.p+h_B(u)]/2
                  <[h_A(u)+h_B(u)]/2<=h_K(u).

The strict inequalities persist for small epsilon, simultaneously
for the finitely many facet normals of K. Every vertex of B outside
F_B also has strict slack in the n inequality at epsilon=0 and stays
inside K for sufficiently small epsilon. The remaining vertices are
exactly those of F_B, giving the new segment in (4). This proves (4)
without selecting a smaller middle growth profile.

In the tangential coordinate on F_K, J lies STRICTLY inside F_K.
In fact it already lies strictly inside I_0: its endpoint gaps there
are half of the two positive distances from p to the endpoints of
F_A. Its small translate therefore satisfies every other facet
inequality of K. Consequently K_epsilon minus K is exactly the
trapezoid with base F_K and top J+epsilon n/2, apart from its base.
When L_B=0 this trapezoid is a triangle.

The added areas are exactly

    |A_epsilon|-|A|=epsilon L_A/2,
    |K_epsilon|-|K|=epsilon(L_K/4+L_B/8),
    M_epsilon-M=epsilon D,
    D=L_A/2+L_K/4+L_B/8.                             (5)

## 3. Exact first-order cost with the whole middle face

Let T_p^A be the unit-height tent on F_A with peak p. On F_K choose
a unit tangential coordinate, write its endpoints as a<b, and write
the endpoints of J as c<=d. Thus a<c<=d<b. Define its unit-height
trapezoidal profile by

    H_J(s)=(s-a)/(c-a),             a<=s<=c,
            1,                     c<=s<=d,
            (b-s)/(b-d),           d<=s<=b.           (6)

It is an ordinary tent if c=d. Since all the original cuts on A,K
are proper, none is a supporting-face line. Integrating the actual
thin triangles and trapezoids gives each cap increment to first order
by its original face signature. The added middle height is epsilon/2,
so the common moving-menu budget satisfies

    q_epsilon=Q+epsilon q'+o(epsilon),
    q'=integral_(F_A) T_p^A W_A ds
                   +(1/2)integral_(F_K) H_J W_K ds.  (7)

For completeness, this uses the same actual implicit meeting-point
argument as the face-tent source: the original budget map has rows
-s_i v_i in the y coordinates and -1 in the common-budget coordinate.
Its Jacobian is invertible. The actual added-cap functions have size
O(epsilon) and Lipschitz constants O(epsilon) in the nearby meeting
point, because every nonparallel cut meets each thin band in length
O(epsilon); a parallel proper cut is separated from that band. The
inverse-map contraction argument supplies a genuine y_epsilon in
int K and a common budget. Multiplying its first-order equations by
1/s_i proves (7). No displayed normal is presumed to stay critical.

The exact normalized first-order cost is therefore

    C_coupled(p)=C_A(p)+C_K(p),
    C_A(p)=integral_(F_A) T_p^A(W_A-r) ds,
    C_K(p)=(1/2)integral_(F_K) H_J(W_K-r) ds.         (8)

If Q is the original GLOBAL maximum raw depth and the ordinary
endpoint maximum m_A<Q, then C_coupled(p)<0 gives actual strict
normalized-depth descent. Indeed the new middle fiber, including
its new points, is covered by the moving cap menu. The new A ordinary
maximum is at most m_A+epsilon L_A/2 and keeps its gap. The unchanged
endpoint has m_B<=Q, while q'>0 by positivity of the two cap loads;
thus a tied B maximum is also below the new menu for small epsilon.
Finally

    q_epsilon/M_epsilon-Q/M
          =(epsilon/M) C_coupled(p)+o(epsilon).

This keeps the whole actual K face; its outer portions are not
discarded merely because the endpoint Minkowski face is shorter.

An optional exact evaluation reduces its trapezoidal integral to two
tent integrals on that SAME F_K. Let T_c,T_d be tents on [a,b] with
the indicated peaks. Direct comparison of their three affine pieces
gives

    H_J=[(b-c)/(b-a)]T_c+[(d-a)/(b-a)]T_d.           (9)

The coefficients sum to 1+(d-c)/(b-a), as required for its plateau;
they are not normalized probabilities. Formula (9), combined with
the finite step-function formulas in the face-tent source, evaluates
every original cap signature exactly.

## 4. A proved compensation bound and the larger-face penalty

There is a useful actual comparison with the A tent cost. Put

    Delta=L_K-(L_A+L_B)/2>=0.

Assume p lies on none of the original A cutting lines, so W_A(p)
has an actual strict signature. Then

    C_coupled(p) <= (5/4)C_A(p)
           +(L_B/4)(W_A(p)-r)+((1-r)/4)Delta.        (10)

To prove it, first replace the whole F_K temporarily by the ACTUAL
contained interval I_0=(F_A+F_B)/2, keeping the same top J. Its added
trapezoid is exactly the midpoint sum of the actual added A triangle
with the segment F_B. The replacement is used only for a comparison;
the difference to the actual K addition will be paid below.

At every fixed normal height in the A triangle, its tangential
section is an interval [l(h),r(h)] containing the coordinate of p.
Adding F_B=[b_-,b_+] partitions its interval sum into three disjoint
pieces, up to endpoints:

    [l(h)+b_-, p+b_-],
    [p+b_-, p+b_+],
    [p+b_+, r(h)+b_+].

The first and third pieces are translations of the left and right
parts of the A interval by ACTUAL endpoints of F_B. The middle
piece pairs the vertical A point above p with all points of F_B.
These row partitions integrate to actual disjoint sets.

For ANY such paired points x_A and x_B in B, capture of their
midpoint in the i-th original middle cap implies

    v_i.x_A >=2v_i.y_0-v_i.x_B
                    >=2v_i.y_0-h_i=b_i.

Thus W_K((x_A+x_B)/2)<=W_A(x_A), pointwise, and subtracting r
preserves the inequality. Area scales by 1/4 under the midpoint map.
The two translated pieces therefore contribute at most one quarter
of the A triangle's cost. In the middle strip, the vertical A points
above p keep its strict signature for small epsilon, and that strip
has area epsilon L_B before midpoint scaling. Dividing by epsilon
gives the inner middle cost bound

    C_K,inner(p) <= C_A(p)/4+(L_B/4)(W_A(p)-r).     (11)

The actual profile on the larger face F_K dominates the profile on
I_0 pointwise, with the same plateau J. This follows directly on
each ramp: extending its zero endpoint outward increases the height
at every old position and adds nonnegative height outside. Their
added-area derivative difference is exactly Delta/4, by (5) applied
to the two base lengths. Since W_K-r<=1-r, its contribution to the
actual middle cost is at most (1-r)Delta/4. Adding the A cost proves
(10). This pays the full actual outer-face addition rather than
choosing an artificially smaller growth profile.

Two concrete scoped consequences are immediate:

* If F_K=(F_A+F_B)/2, C_A(p)<0, and p is in a strict A cap-sign
  region of load W_A(p)<r, then C_coupled(p)<0.
* If additionally F_B is a point, the same conclusion follows from
  C_A(p)<0 alone; no strict signature at p is needed, because the
  middle strip in the proof has zero area.

More generally the explicit inequality

    5C_A(p)+L_B(W_A(p)-r)+(1-r)Delta<0

is a sufficient condition for coupled descent under the global-Q and
m_A<Q assumptions above. No bound on Delta, automatic negativity,
or classification of all shared support faces is claimed.

## 5. An actual signed-roof variation removes outer-face excess

One may instead use a different ACTUAL compatible middle polygon,
which trims the outer portions of its old face while adding the inner
trapezoid. This is a continuous admissible path, not a substitution of
a smaller cap-growth profile in (3).

Use tangential coordinate s and normal coordinate
t=n.x-h_K(n) on the middle face. Write

    F_K=[a,b], I_0=[a_0,b_0], J=[c,d],
    a<=a_0<c<=d<b_0<=b.

Keep every facet inequality of K except t<=0. Replace that one by
the following THREE actual inequalities:

    t<=epsilon/2,
    t<= (epsilon/2)(s-a_0)/(c-a_0),
    t<= (epsilon/2)(b_0-s)/(b_0-d).                  (12)

Call the resulting polygon K_epsilon^s. On the old face its signed
normal displacement profile is (epsilon/2)G(s), where

    G(s)=min{1,(s-a_0)/(c-a_0),(b_0-s)/(b_0-d)}.      (13)

This is positive on the inner interval I_0, zero at its endpoints,
and negative on the outer excess. In particular it removes a real
layer there; the original K is not falsely declared unchanged.

For sufficiently small epsilon the path is compatible:

    (A_epsilon+B)/2 subset K_epsilon^s.              (14)

To prove this using finite exact geometry, put D=(A+B)/2. Its face
in direction n is EXACTLY I_0, by equality in (1) and the exposed-face
identity for a Minkowski sum. Every vertex of D outside I_0 has a
fixed negative t-coordinate and therefore satisfies (12) for small
epsilon; all face points in I_0 satisfy it because G>=0 there.
The other new seed is (p+epsilon n+B)/2. Its vertices corresponding
to F_B are J at height epsilon/2 and satisfy (12). Each other vertex
has a fixed negative limiting t-coordinate and also satisfies (12)
for small epsilon. All seed points satisfy the unchanged K facets
by the strict support argument in Section 2. Convexity proves (14).

The new polygons are uniformly bounded and converge to K. For an
elementary boundedness check, normalize the old facet normals. Their
maximum scalar product with any unit direction has a positive minimum,
since K is bounded. Replacing its n normal by one of the nearby
normals in (12) preserves half that positive bound for small epsilon;
the right sides stay bounded. Every point of int K is eventually in
the new polygon, while every limit point satisfies all old facet
inequalities. These observations also give the claimed convergence
and preserve a fixed neighborhood of the source y_0.

The signed area and cap first variations are exactly the integrals
of G on the whole F_K. Away from its endpoints, the other facets
have strict slack, so the new upper boundary is given by (12).
Near each endpoint, intersection with its fixed nonparallel adjacent
facet moves by O(epsilon). The remaining corner correction has both
width and height O(epsilon), hence area O(epsilon^2). This argument
uses the finite polygon edges with redundant collinear inequalities
removed; it asserts no such rate for general curved boundaries.
Proper original cuts have at most one intersection with F_K, so the
same estimate applies to their signed cap increments. Consequently

    M_epsilon^s-M=epsilon D_s+o(epsilon),
    D_s=L_A/2+(1/2)integral_(F_K)G(s) ds,
    q_epsilon^s=Q+epsilon q_s'+o(epsilon),
    q_s'=integral_(F_A)T_p^A W_A ds
                    +(1/2)integral_(F_K)G W_K ds,
    C_s=q_s'-r D_s
       =C_A(p)+(1/2)integral_(F_K)G(W_K-r) ds.      (15)

The meeting-point construction remains valid: signed cap increments
have size O(epsilon) and vanishing Lipschitz constants in the source
point, just as in Section 3. All new middle points are bounded by the
actual moving cap menu. This controls the true new maximum even
though portions of K have been removed and other portions added.

## 6. Exact total-mass change and possible endpoint ties

Let the two excess lengths be ell_L=a_0-a and ell_R=b-b_0. Let
d_L,d_R>0 be the distances from p to the endpoints of F_A, so
d_L+d_R=L_A. The corresponding ramp lengths are
c-a_0=d_L/2 and b_0-d=d_R/2. Integration of the two negative linear
extensions in (13) yields

    D_s=5L_A/8+L_B/4
           -ell_L^2/(2d_L)-ell_R^2/(2d_R).          (16)

The positive middle-area coefficient inside I_0 is L_A/8+L_B/4;
the rest of (16) is its REAL removed area, in addition to the A gain.

Assume Q is the original global raw maximum and m_A<Q as before.
If also m_B<Q, then C_s<0 is sufficient for strict normalized
descent, irrespective of the sign of D_s: both endpoint gaps persist.
If m_B=Q, the unchanged B endpoint must be retained. The true new
global upper certificate is the maximum of its fixed raw mass Q and
the moving middle budget, with the separated A endpoint omitted.
Its first-order normalized coefficient is

    max(q_s',0)-r D_s.

Thus in the tied-B case the exact strict first-order sufficient test
is the pair of inequalities

    D_s>0 and C_s<0.                                (17)

They are also necessary for strict negativity of this specified
first-order upper certificate. No descent is claimed when the middle
trim shrinks the denominator while a tied B source remains fixed.

For reference, the largest possible D_s as p varies over the relative
interior of F_A has supremum

    5L_A/8+L_B/4-(ell_L+ell_R)^2/(2L_A).             (18)

This follows from
ell_L^2/d_L+ell_R^2/d_R >=(ell_L+ell_R)^2/L_A.
If both excesses are positive, equality is attained at
d_L:L_A=ell_L:(ell_L+ell_R). A one-sided excess gives the supremum
by approaching the corresponding endpoint. The same p must also
satisfy the cost condition in (17); independently optimal mass and
cost centers cannot be combined.

## 7. A concrete sufficient repair with the actual outer signatures

Suppose C_A(p)<0 and p is in a strict region with W_A(p)<r. Suppose
also that the actual outer portions F_K minus I_0 have W_K>=r
almost everywhere. Because G is negative on those outer portions,
their contribution to the signed cost (15) is nonpositive. The inner
comparison (11) therefore gives

    C_s <=(5/4)C_A(p)+(L_B/4)(W_A(p)-r)<0.           (19)

This repairs an arbitrarily larger middle face at the level of the
menu cost by an ACTUAL compatible change of the middle polygon.
For a tied B endpoint one must additionally check D_s>0, as (16)--(17)
require. Without a tie, both endpoint gaps suffice.

In the planar below-target regime, suppose in addition that the
displayed caps genuinely attain the halfspace depth at y_0. The
audited chord-gauge bound then gives every pair-capture load at
least 1/4>r when r<2/9.
Thus the outer-signature condition holds in particular if each such
outer point is captured by at least two original middle halfspaces.
This incidence is an explicit assumption, not inferred from the
mere excess length. If outer points instead have a low singleton
weight, their negative displacement can have a positive normalized
cost; formula (15) retains it exactly.

The source thus supplies both a full-profile enlargement and a
distinct signed-profile repair, with their actual geometry and source
ownership conditions. It does not assume arbitrary minimizers are
polygons, that every larger face has favorable outer signatures, or
that a tied endpoint disappears.
